items.title: Pilsner Clones
items.text:
Pilsner Clones
I just got a chest freezer and temperature controller and I'm looking to brew a pilsner for a BBQ coming up. I've been looking up LaBatt clones, a lot of my curling buddies are showing up and that seems to be popular in that crowd. The recipe I found for that has about 2:1 Marris Otter and Flaked Barley, with Hallertau Hersbrucker bittering hops and Saaz finishing hops. But I just picked up a bunch of different lagers/pilsners last night and tried Veltins Pilsener for the first time, it is really good. I can't find any clone recipes. I don't like brewing straight clones, but I generally look at the grain and hop bills of a few different recipes online and modify them to match my tastes. I don't brew with enough variety often enough yet to just pick out a grain bill and hop bill by taste, especially when its not an IPA.  


Does anyone who has had Veltins have any suggestions on grain and hop schedules?

I was thinking of doing a decoration mash. I use a drink dispensing cooler with a false bottom as my mash tun, no heating element. I’ve seen people say to decoration mash at like 0.75 water to grain then raise the temp by adding hot water until you get your desired ratio. Is that what you do?

My well water is acidic and high in iron so I generally go with a few 5 gallon jugs of spring water when I brew, like Poland Spring or something. Do you happen to know if that’s close to the desired profile? What effects do the different water chemistries have on flavor, I normally don’t pay attention because my go-it’s are IPAs, Belgians, and porters

I guess I got my terms screwed up. I was just talking about step mashing. I’ve tried using my banjo cooker to maintain temperature and I always just end up burning stuff. I may try decoction mash later down the line, but not for my first lager batch.

I mean, the bottle says “Canadian Pilsner”, but I get your point. Like I said, I wasn’t going to direct clone anything. I’ve never done a Pilsner, and looking at recipes I didn’t really have any reference for what the chosen hops taste like. I’ve only done Hallertau in porters, never heard of Saaz or many of the others. But it sounds like hops are less important than chosen malt or even water chem. Nevertheless, different pilsners taste different for a reason. Just trying to get a handle on identifying what does what to the palette. I’m trying to avoid just accidentally making something good without knowing why it tastes that way.

items.title: First time lagering
items.text:
First time lagering
This is my first time lagering, so I'm just making sure. My measured OG was 1.062 (underestimated my efficiency, was shooting for 1.058). I pitched yeast late Saturday (its currently Monday morning), at about 65 degrees F. I have it sitting in my temperature controlled freezer right now at 52 degrees F. I used WLP802. The airlock isn't bubbling yet. Should it bubble yet? I know lagers go slower than ales, so I don't know if expecting it to bubble already is wrong. Should I just leave it longer? Bring the temperature up until bubbling starts? If necessary, I won't be able to get another thing of yeast until Wednesday.
Should I raise the temperature some or just wait it out? Do I risk letting the yeast get trapped under settling proteins or anything like that?

Thanks for the advice. The brew is for my Memorial Day BBQ. I'm going to wait a couple weeks a brew my Session Belgian Rye IPA too, so if the lager doesn't work it won't be the end of the world. I've just never had to wait so long before finding out if the beer turned out well or not. Not used to the huge time commitment of waiting. It's also the first time I ever did a step infusion, I wonder if that caused the increase in my efficiency.

items.title: First Lager
items.text:
First Lager
I posted about a week and a half ago with questions about lagering, thanks for all the help. I brewed a week ago and just opened the lid to check on my beer. Are lagers still supposed to have a krausen? Mine does, and I thought that wasn't supposed to happen with bottom fermenting. There's also a new smell in the basement but that could be from the new chest freezer itself. My OG was 1.062, and it might be down to 1.060 now, but just barely. I think I underpitched anyway and it took a couple days for the airlock to start bubbling so I'm not too concerned about the slow ferment. I've never had a brew go bad and am just paranoid with this being my first lager, the long wait time to find out is killing me. The brew is for a BBQ, so if I'm going to need to try again, the sooner I know the better. Any reassurance or early alert to a bad beer would be appreciated.
I used WLP802. I had intended to use WLP800 but they were out. My temp controller is set to 52 degrees F

Yeah, end of May, as long as it’s fermenting and not spoiled I’m good on timeline. It’s possible I read the OG low. My float is hard to read, sticks to the sides of the cylinder. I also didn’t really do a starter, so you may need to delay the actual pitch time when figuring the start of fermentation

18-22C is 64-72F. That sounds like an Ale to me. The onlines for this yeast say 50-55, so I’m right in the middle. But my freezer may have too much, I don’t know what to call it, cooling momentum? When it kicks off it drops a couple extra degrees. I might raise the temp a tad
I will have to try that next time. Thanks

It might be a function of where I’ve located the thermal probe. It’s my first time using a temp controller. For ales I would keep the bucket under a blanket under my thermostat and keep the house a couple degrees cooler than usual for a couple weeks, lol

I just taped mine to the side today. It was loosely in place, I tucked the wire into the handle of the bucket so it wouldn’t move. It was still touching or close to it, but taping it should only make it better.

I just had a thought, should I have blocks underneath to keep air space between the floor and the bucket ? Might be a more even cooling
All my other brews have been IPA, Porters, and Belgians. Never really had to rely on lightly roasted malt and mild yeast for the flavor profiles. My recipe was a complete shot in the dark
I did Pilsner (half Belgian half German, just cuz) a bit of Vienna cuz I felt like it, and some cara pils for head. For hops I went with Magnum buttering and Saaz finishing

So, I didn’t do a starter, I normally don’t for ales and it’s fine, but maybe not so much for lagers. I used a hydrometer. I was shooting for a lower OG but I think I got a big efficiency bump from doing a step infusion mash.

Didn’t do a starter. Just pitched from the pouch. Works every time with my ales. Lesson learned next time for lagers. But there’s definitely a Krausen and bubbles. My guess right now is I was good enough with sterilization that nothing outworked my yeast and it just needed time to self start.

I’m going to have to look up all this starter cell count math, never dealt with it before

I do not remember the date. Our local brew supply is normally pretty good on fresh ingredients, but they are moving locations this month (got a good deal on a 7 gallon glass carboy), so it’s possible it was an older batch of yeast.

If there’s currently a krausen would repitching do anything?
It was liquid. I’m guessing our brew shop is closed on Easter Sunday, which means I can’t get mor yeast until Wednesday morning. If there’s a krausen, isn’t it already started?
I have to wait until at least Wednesday to buy another yeast packet. Do you think it would be worth making a starter on Wednesday and pitching more yeast?
Yay Amazon Prime, it says it’ll be here tomorrow. Thanks for the yeast recommendation
Bring the temp up in general or to help the current underpitched yeast batch?
A float. I have one of those scope ones but I read once you hop it those aren’t accurate anymore
Just pitched the two packets. Checked the OG beforehand, it was down to about 1.044 before the pitch
